Human-first, AI-optional

SoushAI analysis. Drafted by Soushi's AI assistant, reviewed and shared by Soushi.

Tibi, this page picks up our discussion about branch previews in the design system and the broader point you raised: that Soushi tends to think as an engineer and build for AI more than for humans, when Nondominium should stay simple and open to contributors who are less technical or who work without AI. Soushi agrees with most of it and still sees value in clean, idiomatic workflows. The page puts both views side by side and ends on questions for the two of us.

Soushi has answered the questions first: ★ marks his pick, with his reasons. Every card is still open for yours: pick an option, add a note, pin a comment on anything with "comment on…", and use the closing box for anything else. "copy my answers" exports only what you changed, ready to send back. Your answers stay in your browser until you send them.

Humans are the floor.
AI is a floor above it.Everything needed to understand, run, review and merge Nondominium should work with git, a browser and a text editor. AI tooling (pai/, skills, agent files) reads from that floor and speeds it up; nothing on the floor depends on it.

2The case: branch previews

Where the disagreement became concrete. Tibi proposed an experimental page in the design system that shows work in progress on other branches; Soushi proposed showing several chosen branches, not one, and Tibi agreed. They split on how a branch gets chosen.

already worksmodel to copyhow you workideagotcha
The platform already does half of itCloudflare Pages gives every deployed branch its own alias, <branch>.nondominium-design.pages.dev. PR #10's workflow deploys only master with --branch master; widening the trigger to every branch and passing the branch name gives each one a preview URL with no label and no new term.Tibi's version costs a few lines in a workflow that already exists.
Exploring is not shippingA starting design is worth having. It can live as a short design note or an ADR in the repo, ready to apply, without being the thing that ships. Both instincts get their due: the exploration is kept, the code stays minimal.
Where Soushi hesitatesSetting aside a clean, idiomatic practice for contributors who are not here yet feels like a loss, and a PR label is basic git. The narrower point to weigh: not whether labels are hard, but whether this one solves a problem we have had.
The label becomes a filter, not a rewriteIf the page lists branches from the GitHub API, a later whitelist is one label:preview filter on the same list. Starting simple does not close the door on the clean design; it postpones it to the day someone needs it.The idiomatic version stays on paper, the seam for it stays in the code.
"All branches" is not free eitherThe repo squash-merges and delete_branch_on_merge is off. Six of the eight non-master branches on origin belong to PRs already merged, and git cannot tell (squash leaves no ancestry). A naive list shows six finished branches as work in progress.The simple version needs one GitHub setting turned on, plus deleting six stale branches once. Still no new vocabulary.
already worksgotcha
What wrangler already doeswrangler pages deploy build --project-name nondominium-design --branch master uploads the built site as a deployment tagged with a branch. master is the production branch, so it serves nondominium-design.pages.dev and the custom domain. Any other --branch value becomes a preview with its own alias. Per-branch previews need two changes: run the workflow on every branch, and pass the branch name instead of master.
design.sensorica.co for previews?Cloudflare can pin a custom domain to a branch only through a proxied Cloudflare DNS record; through an external DNS the alias falls back to production. sensorica.co stays at GoDaddy (PR #10), so branch.design.sensorica.co would show production. What works today: the experimental page lives on design.sensorica.co and links to each <branch>.nondominium-design.pages.dev.Per-branch subdomains under sensorica.co would mean moving its DNS to Cloudflare.

3Progressive workflow adoption

Soushi's answer to your point, from his first-round comments: good engineering practice is not over-engineering, but nobody has to adopt all of it on day one.

I don't consider good engineer practices as overengineering, but I understand that not all contributors have the technical level to follow them. Having a progressive workflows adoption learning curve would be nice. (Soushi, 2026-10-09)

already worksmodel to copyidearisk
The invariantWhatever the rung, a change lands through a reviewed PR. Soushi named this as the one thing a lighter workflow keeps.
Same shape as Sensorica's content rulesTibi's paper restates them: add without permission (Rule 3), polish style without permission (Rule 4), never delete, negotiate in discussion. Low friction to add, care where it matters.
Open to trainingSoushi wants contributors open to good practice. The ladder makes that a path with steps, not a test at the door.
A ladder can read as a rankIf rungs look like status, newcomers feel second-class. Name them by the tools they add, never by the person.

4Your paper: stigmergic co-creation

Stigmergic Co-Creation in the Age of AI uses the Nondominium merges as its case: local AI agents resolving conflicts silently subtracted each other's work. Several of its points touch this board directly.

already worksmodel to copyidea
ADRs in bothPrinciple 2 lists Architecture or Agent Decision Records as a signal file. The label ADR Soushi picked below is the same practice.
Agent files are shared governance tooPrinciple 1: repositories carry AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .rules files so that every contributor's local agent loads the network's rules. The root agent file is where shared rules reach other people's AI, not only Soushi's tooling.Supports one real AGENTS.md that everyone's agent reads.
Documentation-first precedenceAt a merge, specifications and planning docs take precedence over transient code, citing Nondominium's documentation-first workflow.
Structure, placed where nobody has to learn itThe paper proposes three git gates and shared signal servers: real machinery. The gates run in shared CI, so a contributor meets them only when a change subtracts. Same test as the ladder: complexity is fine where newcomers do not have to carry it.

5Two views

Both are partly right. The onboarding methodology already named the meeting point in May, for the docs; it was never applied to code and workflows.

already worksmodel to copyhow you workidearisk
Where they meetFrom the methodology draft: réduire la friction, pas le contenu. Several doors in, with the real complexity still reachable behind them.Layering and a complexity budget, not a downgrade.
Soushi's pointIdiomatic structure, strong types and AI workflows help two part-time volunteers keep a Holochain codebase sane. Making the code look simple by making it worse would hurt everyone.Simplicity should not mean removing the advanced workflow for those who use it.
The NRP lesson, in Tibi's wordsOn 2026-09-29: NRP's universal language "polluait un peu, les gens se trouvaient aliénés". The vocabulary of our tooling can alienate the same way the vocabulary of the ontology does.
Too opinionated about workflows?Soushi's own question. Branch model, worktrees, stacked PRs, PR template sections and commit scopes are all opinions a newcomer has to adopt before a first contribution. Being opinionated for oneself is fine; what matters is how much of it the project requires of others.Split how each of us works from what the project requires, and keep the second list short.
Tibi's pointThe project reads as built for an engineer with an AI agent: hundreds of lines of agent instructions at the root, worktrees, stacked PRs, generated rule trees. A Sensorica member who is not a developer, or a developer without an AI assistant, bounces.The cost is contributors who never arrive, so nobody sees them leave.

Already in place
  • Discussions and Wiki are both enabled on GitHub.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md already says worktrees are optional and plain git checkout works.
  • AI files are generated from pai/ by nix develop and gitignored, so they never show up in diffs.
Where the AI layer leaks into the floor
  • CONTRIBUTING.md has a full section on AI tooling conventions and none on "your first contribution".
  • Three near-identical agent files (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md) sit beside the README.
  • The README opens on "ValueFlows-compliant multi-DNA Holochain hApp", not on the human problem.

7The layer model

The floor is what any contributor needs. The AI layer is what lets whoever uses it go faster. The arrow only goes one way.

8Principles to test

Candidates, not decisions. Each should survive the question "does this stop either of us from working the way we work?"

idearisk
The deletion testDelete pai/, .claude/, .cursor/, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md. The project must still be understandable, buildable, reviewable and mergeable.A concrete, checkable definition of AI-optional.
Idiomatic is not a reason on its ownAn idiom earns its place when it removes a real, repeated problem. "It's how it's done" names the norm, not the need.
The reviewer testIf a co-maintainer cannot review a PR without an AI explaining it, the PR is too clever or too big. The PR body carries the explanation, not the AI.
Root is for humansTop-level files are the front door. Agent files there should be short pointers, not long manuals.
Two layers driftIf the AI layer documents things the human docs do not, knowledge moves to where only agents read it.Facts live on the floor; pai/ only points at them.
Personal tools stay personalEach contributor's own workflow (worktrees, AI planning notes, stacked PRs) is welcome, as long as it never becomes a requirement for others.

10Questions for us

The first three are about branch previews, then the project in general, then three new questions from Soushi's answers. ★ marks Soushi's pick; pick freely and say why in the note.

decided

1. First version of the branch preview page?

nondominium-design-system: PR #10 deploys master to Cloudflare Pages. The experimental page shows work in progress on other branches. Tibi prefers no new label or term; Soushi first proposed an opt-in PR label.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: the simple floor now, the label idea kept in writing.

decided

2. Turn on delete-branch-on-merge in the design-system repo?

The setting is off and PRs are squash-merged, so 6 of the 8 non-master branches on origin are finished work that still looks open.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: removes the main reason for a whitelist, at no cost to anyone.

decided

3. Where does the label idea live?

Soushi sees the label version as a clean starting design worth exploring; Tibi sees it as premature.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: a short ADR in the design-system repo.

decided

4. Write "human-first, AI-optional" into CONTRIBUTING?

Today the principle exists only in conversation. Nondominium is the first case; R&O and hREA could follow.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick, and he also wants it as a rule for his own AI assistant in every public repo.

decided

5. What happens to the agent files at the root?

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are 236 lines each and largely duplicate one another; REVIEW.md adds 152. They sit beside README.md.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick, with a question: keep one source and make the others symlinks to it? See the first new card.

decided

6. Which test defines "complexity only when needed"?

A test makes it checkable in review instead of a matter of taste.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: the reviewer test gates every PR, the rule of three guides refactoring.

decided

7. First concrete move on Nondominium?

The onboarding methodology's roadmap is still on paper. Discussions and Wiki are on. 0 of 61 open issues are labelled for newcomers.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: the smallest step a newcomer actually meets.

decided

8. Change the PR template?

The template has Intent, Changes, Decisions, How to test, Documentation, Related, all at the same level.

★ my lean, because Soushi's pick: introduce the PR clearly first, everything else in a collapsible Details section.

decided

9. Where does the single agent-instructions file live?

Decided: one AGENTS.md, the others point to it. Soushi's open question: the source should sit in pai/ with symlinks. Git's docs: with core.symlinks false (set on some Windows checkouts) a symlink is checked out as a small text file holding the path.

decided

10. How many rungs on the contribution ladder?

Progressive adoption, with a reviewed PR at every rung.

decided

11. How does someone move up a rung?

The ladder must invite, not gatekeep.
